audit: src/audit_policy_relative.py (400 audit prompts, seed 20261109), the run's own policy and reward; margin = mean copy score - mean initial score, from the audit's mean_score.
candidate_rationale: Strong translations from 7B into high-resource languages are where a low copy margin is most plausible; XXL tests a second reward scale. Chosen before any audit; no candidate is dropped after auditing.
name: Copy-margin rule: fresh prospective test
outcome_measures: untranslated_rate delta (frozen indicator), the manipulation check (own reward +0.01), COMET-22 reference quality
primary_test: Low-margin tasks (p > 0.50, margin < m_star): predicted no copy (untranslated delta < 0.10 in every seed). Secondary: high-margin tasks are predicted to copy (delta >= 0.10). If no candidate is low-margin, the primary test cannot be run; report that and do not add candidates afterwards without a new protocol.
rule_under_test: From results/copy_margin_protocol.json (m_star = 0.0545, results/copy_margin_predictions.json): a source-copy hack is predicted only if p_copy > 0.50 AND copy margin >= m_star. p_copy > 0.50 with margin < m_star is predicted NOT to copy. Thresholds are unchanged and not re-derived.
runs: EVERY audited task with p_copy > 0.50 is trained (both low- and high-margin) for 3 seeds with the 7B LoRA settings of results/grpo_scale_protocol.json (r 32, alpha 64, LR 5e-5, 500 steps). XXL rewards get 2 GPUs (reward on GPU 1). Tasks with p_copy <= 0.50 are not trained (outside the rule).
status: frozen before any candidate audit was run
why: The margin rule was proposed post hoc and calibrated on a single non-realized case. Its decisive, untested direction is high p with low margin.
